rationale: Evidence from iteration 10 (score 800.3, best so far). The oval (20/20, 1.90 s, max_error 0.018) and s-bend (19/20, max_error 0.032) are solved. The slalom is the only failing track: 8/20 finished, 12 off-track, progress 0.80, up from 0.64 at kp 3.2. Each steering-gain step on the 16 mm footprint has raised slalom progress (kp 2.6 to 3.2 gave 0.31 to 0.64, kp 3.2 to 3.6 gave 0.64 to 0.80), and line_loss_events on the slalom stayed low (0.35). So steering authority is still the limit, not sensing or speed. Slalom steering_oscillation rose to 0.45 and control_effort to 16.6, but oval oscillation is only 0.18, so there is margin. Change: raise kp from 3.6 to 4.0 for more correction per unit of signal, and raise kd from 1.3 to 1.5 to keep the damping ratio near the 0.36 that gave clean oval and s-bend results and to control the rising slalom jitter. Geometry, sensor weights, base_speed 0.85, ki 0 and last_direction line loss are unchanged, so the gain step is isolated. Expected result: slalom progress about 0.85 to 0.9 with more finishes (about 10 to 14 of 20), oval and s-bend still at or above about 940. Risk: slalom oscillation may pass 0.5 and cut the finish rate. If it does, the next step is kd about 1.8 rather than lowering base_speed, because finishing is worth far more than the small time term. Hypotheses for the next race: (a) if slalom progress reaches about 0.9 but still ends off track, the limit is speed through the sharpest bends, so base_speed should drop to about 0.75; (b) if oval steering_oscillation exceeds 0.3, kd is too low and should rise to about 1.8; (c) if slalom line_loss_events rise above 0.5, the 16 mm footprint is overlapping background on sharp bends and 12 mm should be retested with these gains. Measurements requested: all available measurements, so per-track progress, max_error, oscillation and line-loss counts can be compared with iteration 10.
